newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Down on bearish trade, Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas -Down on bearish trade, Taiwan.

text.p: Gasoline prices fell on aggressive selling and lower-than-expected awards into Taiwan's reformate tender, traders said on Wednesday.

Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) bought "more than one" 250,000-barrel cargoes of 95-octane unleaded reformate for March 16-30 delivery at around $27.90 per barrel on a cost-and-freight basis, a company official said.
"It is too low ... it looks very aggressive," complained one trader.
Most offers into the tender were heard around $29.00, traders said.
The CPC official would not comment on the exact number of cargoes or the winners.
The tender sought offers on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Keelung, Taichung, Kaohisung or Shalung by February 18 and was be valid until February 20.
CPC's purchase of unleaded reformate was even higher than its last record purchase, for one cargo for March 1-15 at $27.60 per barrel c-and-f.

"The market is still very tight... in view of the shutdowns. The Mideast is also tight and India does not normally buy so many cargoes," said one western trader on the two refinery shutdowns in Singapore in March and India's purchases of 90,000 tonnes for March 1-15 delivery.
Naphtha prices edged up on firmer swaps, although on the physical, traders were focussing on the Kuwaiti term talks for March 1997-February 1998 supplies.
Traders said Kuwait was asking for bids of $15 per tonne over Mideast naphtha spot quotes, almost double from term prices agreed in August at a $7.90 premium.

In the Singapore market, both a Dutch trader and a Japanese trader was agggressively offering a 50,000-barrel cargo of 92-octane unleaded gasoline lifting March at $26.80-$27.20 per barrel fob Singapore.
A Singapore trader emerged late afternoon to bid for March 6-10 liftings of the same grade at $26.20, later raising it to $26.35, where the Dutch trader matched the bid.
Traders said the deal level was low and did not reflect fundamentals.
"It (the $15 premium) is achievable if there's really a short and the market is tight," said one term buyer. "But the Japanese will find that a high price to pay."
March naphtha swaps were traded at $24.00 per barrel between a Japanese trader and a European major. Levels were last quoted at $23.90/$24.10, up 10 cents from Tuesday.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
